newsitem.title: FRANCE: French poll shows smaller centre-right majority.
newsitem.headline: French poll shows smaller centre-right majority.

text.p: France's centre-right coalition holds a comfortable lead over the left-wing opposition in the race for next month's parliamentary election but stands to sees its majority reduced, an opinion poll released on Sunday showed.

The Sofres poll for Monday's Le Figaro newspaper showed the RPR-UDF coalition and other conservatives winning around 329 seats, the Socialists, other left and ecologists 202, the Communists 23 and the extreme-right National Front one of the 555 seats in metropolitan France.

The RPR-UDF parties held 464 seats before President Jacques Chirac dissolved the 577-seat National Assembly last Monday and called a snap two-round parliamentary election for May 25 and June 1. Coalition supporters hold most of the 22 seats in France's overseas departments and territories.

Sofres based its projection on a sample of 1,000 adults polled on Friday and Saturday. The survey showed some 35 percent planned to vote RPR-UDF and five percent for other conservatives in the first round, 28 percent for the Socialists plus 1.5 percent for other left candidates, 14 percent for the National Front, nine percent for the Communists, five percent for the ecologists and 2.5 percent for the extreme left.
Some 54 percent thought the Socialists were not ready to govern.

An IFOP poll published in Sunday's Journal du Dimanche gave similar results, suggesting the centre-right coalition could be returned with a pared majority of between 311 and 331 seats, with the Socialists taking between 200 and 220.
